canonical.name: Floating-point CG can lose the exact residual orthogonality, $A$-conjugacy, and finite-termination properties proved in exact arithmetic
The preconditioned CG estimate is the ordinary Chebyshev CG bound applied to the symmetrically transformed operator $C^{-1}AC^{-*}$
The Hermitian positive-definite quadratic energy $\phi(x)=\tfrac12\langle Ax,x\rangle-\operatorname{Re}\langle b,x\rangle$ is the optimization functional behind the page's CG route.
For Hermitian positive-definite $A$, solving $Ax=b$ is equivalent to uniquely minimizing the quadratic energy.
The Hermitian positive-definite Krylov Galerkin iterate is the affine-space candidate whose residual is orthogonal to the Krylov space.
Galerkin residual orthogonality is exactly $A$-orthogonality of the error, and it characterizes the iterate uniquely.
Lanczos is Arnoldi specialized to a Hermitian matrix with the standard real-subdiagonal phase convention.
